definition.en: A model of disability that conceives disability as a defective or pathological condition of the individual, inevitably entailing disadvantages both at the personal level and at the relational and social levels, and which must therefore be “treated” and, where possible, “repaired” through the instruments of medicine and technology, taking as its standard reference a presumed normal state of health and human functioning.

en: Although it has never been the subject of a genuine theoretical elaboration, this paradigm has most profoundly permeated the narratives and practices surrounding disability (including legal ones) and continues to find implicit legitimisation within them, despite giving rise to deep-seated ableist prejudices and manifest forms of discrimination.
